title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-04-14
content:
Attendees: Aisha Patel (notes), Marco Hernandez, Samantha Li, Jon Park, Priya Rao, Erin Cole (SRE)

Agenda:
- Quick summary of latest regression alerts
- Test-run results (staging + stress-prod) from 2026-04-13
- Investigation findings and hypothesis (kernel selection, batching, KV cache)
- Action items and owners

Summary:
We observed a ~1.8x P99 latency regression and ~35% throughput drop on the H100 pool for our standard text-gen workload starting 2026-04-12 03:00 UTC. Alert triggered by the perf-alerting pipeline (JIRA-ENG-4821). On initial triage, regression correlated with two changes deployed during the 2026-04-12 deploy window: PR #5872 (kernel selector fallback tweak) and a config roll for default batching window (reduced from 20ms to 12ms) in canary. Both rolled to prod via the normal rollout; canary signals were noisy.

Key metrics (baseline vs current) - H100, seq_len=1024, batch sizing workload A (1000 concurrent small requests):
- P50 latency: baseline 110ms -> current 140ms
- P95 latency: baseline 160ms -> current 260ms
- P99 latency: baseline 220ms -> current 390ms
- Sustained throughput: baseline ~150 req/s -> current ~95 req/s
- KV-cache hit rate: baseline 18% -> current 9% (observed on request traces)

Test runs performed:
- Staging run (A100): no significant regression (p99 within 10% of baseline). Suggests hardware-specific kernel path on H100.
- H100 stress-prod sim (isolated pool): reproduced regression consistently with PR #5872 enabled. Reverting PR config in the pool restored baseline numbers.
- Batching window A/B: increasing batching window back to 20ms recovered ~15% throughput but did not fully restore p99.
- Disabled the kernel selector fallback (force old selector) in a test cluster: p99 returned to baseline.

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
1) Kernel selector fallback tweak (PR #5872) introduces a non-optimal path for certain attention kernel sizes on H100 leading to higher per-token compute time. Reproduction and comparisons show a different set of kernels used for sequence lengths ~512-1536.
2) Reduced batching window reduced effective batching opportunities under bursty traffic pattern, increasing per-request overhead and causing KV cache hit amplification issues. Lower KV cache hits amplified work per request.
3) Combined effect (suboptimal kernel + smaller batching window) created worst-case scenario on H100, accounting for observed ~35% throughput drop.
4) A100 is less sensitive because kernel coverage / fallback differs; selector change primarily impacted H100 patterns.

Logs and traces:
- Sample trace ids: trace-20260413-01, trace-20260413-17 (attached to the JIRA ticket)
- Observed increased memcpy times and additional kernel launch overhead in the H100 traces (detailed flame charts linked in JIRA).

Immediate actions taken during meeting:
- Rolled back PR #5872 in prod H100 pool (canary already rolled back earlier).
- Temporarily increased batching window to 25ms in H100 test pool to evaluate tail improvements.
- Added a short-term alert to monitor KV cache hit rate drop below 12% (threshold) across prod pools.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Marco: write a small repro harness to compare kernel selection paths across A100/H100 and collect microbenchmarks (ETA: 2026-04-16).
- Samantha: open a follow-up PR that restores previous kernel selector as default and adds opt-in for new selector behind an H100-only flag + integration test (PR draft by 2026-04-15).
- Jon: evaluate batching policy heuristics to make window adaptive to observed QPS (prototype by 2026-04-20).
- Priya: instrument KV cache telemetry to emit per-request cache eligibility and hit/miss tags in traces (ETA: 2026-04-17).
- Erin (SRE): coordinate safe rollback plan and monitor alerts; escalate to on-call if p99 > 300ms for >10 minutes (ongoing).

Longer term / product notes:
- Need to add H100-specific kernel validation during model onboarding and have a test matrix that includes H100 microbenchmarks for fallback selector changes.
- Consider more conservative rollout policy for kernel selection changes (start in isolated H100 pool + ramp with synthetic load).
- Revisit default batching window; default 20ms was chosen to balance latency/throughput but dynamic adaptive window could provide better tail behavior.

Open questions:
- Why did canary signals not flag this earlier? Canary traffic profile may not be representative; need to expand canary scenarios.
- Are there other PRs touching CUDA kernel invocation patterns in the same deploy window? Search ongoing.

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Target: perf-benchmarking-sync 2026-04-16 (deep dive on microbenchmarks). Marco to present kernels comparison.
- Will update JIRA-ENG-4821 with experimental results and link PRs.

Attachments / links:
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-4821
- PR (candidate): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5872
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1712345678901

Notes to self: keep meeting notes lightweight; attach flame charts and microbench CSVs to JIRA. If we see reoccurrence after rollback, escalate to on-call lead and consider rolling other runtime optimizations behind feature gates.
